claim: Individuals with Down syndrome (DS) display clear signs of immune dysregulation, including high rates of autoimmunity and severe complications from infections.
source: Individuals with Down syndrome (DS), the genetic condition caused by trisomy 21 (T21), display clear signs of immune dysregulation, including high rates of autoimmunity and severe complications from infections.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a background statement and is supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: T21 causes increased interferon responses and JAK/STAT signaling.
source: Although it is well established that T21 causes increased interferon responses and JAK/STAT signaling, elevated autoantibodies, global immune remodeling, and hypercytokinemia, the interplay between these processes, the clinical manifestations of DS, and potential therapeutic interventions remain ill defined.
evidence: This is stated as well-established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: T21 causes elevated autoantibodies.
source: Although it is well established that T21 causes increased interferon responses and JAK/STAT signaling, elevated autoantibodies, global immune remodeling, and hypercytokinemia, the interplay between these processes, the clinical manifestations of DS, and potential therapeutic interventions remain ill defined.
evidence: This is stated as well-established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: T21 causes global immune remodeling.
source: Although it is well established that T21 causes increased interferon responses and JAK/STAT signaling, elevated autoantibodies, global immune remodeling, and hypercytokinemia, the interplay between these processes, the clinical manifestations of DS, and potential therapeutic interventions remain ill defined.
evidence: This is stated as well-established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: T21 causes hypercytokinemia.
source: Although it is well established that T21 causes increased interferon responses and JAK/STAT signaling, elevated autoantibodies, global immune remodeling, and hypercytokinemia, the interplay between these processes, the clinical manifestations of DS, and potential therapeutic interventions remain ill defined.
evidence: This is stated as well-established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Multi-organ autoimmunity of pediatric onset occurs concurrently with unexpected autoantibody-phenotype associations in DS.
source: We demonstrate multi-organ autoimmunity of pediatric onset concurrent with unexpected autoantibody-phenotype associations in DS.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: Constitutive immune remodeling and hypercytokinemia occur from an early age prior to autoimmune diagnoses or autoantibody production.
source: Importantly, constitutive immune remodeling and hypercytokinemia occur from an early age prior to autoimmune diagnoses or autoantibody production.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: The first 10 participants to complete 16 weeks of tofacitinib treatment showed a good safety profile with no serious adverse events.
source: Analysis of the first 10 participants to complete 16 weeks of tofacitinib treatment shows a good safety profile and no serious adverse events.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the clinical trial stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 4.

claim: Tofacitinib treatment reduced skin pathology in alopecia areata, psoriasis, and atopic dermatitis.
source: Treatment reduced skin pathology in alopecia areata, psoriasis, and atopic dermatitis, while decreasing interferon scores, cytokine scores, and levels of pathogenic autoantibodies without overt immune suppression.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the clinical trial stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: Tofacitinib treatment decreased interferon scores.
source: Treatment reduced skin pathology in alopecia areata, psoriasis, and atopic dermatitis, while decreasing interferon scores, cytokine scores, and levels of pathogenic autoantibodies without overt immune suppression.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the clinical trial stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: Tofacitinib treatment decreased cytokine scores.
source: Treatment reduced skin pathology in alopecia areata, psoriasis, and atopic dermatitis, while decreasing interferon scores, cytokine scores, and levels of pathogenic autoantibodies without overt immune suppression.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the clinical trial stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: Tofacitinib treatment decreased levels of pathogenic autoantibodies without overt immune suppression.
source: Treatment reduced skin pathology in alopecia areata, psoriasis, and atopic dermatitis, while decreasing interferon scores, cytokine scores, and levels of pathogenic autoantibodies without overt immune suppression.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the clinical trial stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: JAK inhibition is a valid strategy to treat autoimmune conditions in DS.
source: JAK inhibition is a valid strategy to treat autoimmune conditions in DS.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the clinical trial results.

claim: Trisomy of human chromosome 21 (T21) occurs at a rate of ~1 in 700 live births.
source: Trisomy of human chromosome 21 (T21) occurs at a rate of ~1 in 700 live births, causing Down syndrome (DS; Lejeune et al., 1959; Antonarakis et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Individuals with DS display developmental delays, stunted growth, cognitive impairments, and increased risk of leukemia, autism spectrum disorders, seizure disorders, and Alzheimer's disease.
source: Individuals with DS display a distinct clinical profile including developmental delays, stunted growth, cognitive impairments, and increased risk of leukemia, autism spectrum disorders, seizure disorders, and Alzheimer's disease (Antonarakis et al., 2020; Chicoine et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: People with DS display widespread immune dysregulation, which manifests through severe complications from respiratory viral infections and high prevalence of myriad immune conditions.
source: People with DS also display widespread immune dysregulation, which manifests through severe complications from respiratory viral infections and high prevalence of myriad immune conditions, including autoimmune thyroid disease (AITD; Iughetti et al., 2014; Pierce et al., 2017; Amr, 2018), celiac disease (Zachor et al., 2000; Book et al., 2001), and skin conditions such as atopic dermatitis, alopecia areata, hidradenitis suppurativa (HS), vitiligo, and psoriasis (Madan et al., 2006; Sureshbabu et al., 2011; Lam et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: People with DS display signs of neuroinflammation from an early age.
source: Furthermore, people with DS display signs of neuroinflammation from an early age (Wilcock and Griffin, 2013; Flores-Aguilar et al., 2020; Araya et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: T21 causes consistent activation of the interferon (IFN) transcriptional response in multiple immune and non-immune cell types with concurrent hypersensitivity to IFN stimulation and hyperactivation of downstream JAK/STAT signaling.
source: We previously reported that T21 causes consistent activation of the interferon (IFN) transcriptional response in multiple immune and non-immune cell types with concurrent hypersensitivity to IFN stimulation and hyperactivation of downstream JAK/STAT signaling (Sullivan et al., 2016; Waugh et al., 2019; Araya et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations to previous work.

claim: Plasma proteomics studies identified dozens of inflammatory cytokines with mechanistic links to IFN signaling that are elevated in people with DS.
source: Plasma proteomics studies identified dozens of inflammatory cytokines with mechanistic links to IFN signaling that are elevated in people with DS (Sullivan et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: T21 drives the production of neurotoxic tryptophan catabolites via the IFN-inducible kynurenine pathway.
source: A large metabolomics study revealed that T21 drives the production of neurotoxic tryptophan catabolites via the IFN-inducible kynurenine pathway (Powers et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Deep immune profiling revealed global immune remodeling with hypersensitivity to IFN across all major branches of the immune system.
source: Deep immune profiling revealed global immune remodeling with hypersensitivity to IFN across all major branches of the immune system (Waugh et al., 2019), and dysregulation of T cell lineages toward a hyperactive, autoimmunity-prone state (Araya et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Four of the six IFN receptors (IFNRs) are encoded on chr21, including Type I, II, and III IFNR subunits.
source: These results could be partly explained by the fact that four of the six IFN receptors (IFNRs) are encoded on chr21, including Type I, II, and III IFNR subunits (Secombes and Zou, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: In a mouse model of DS, normalization of IFNR gene copy number rescues multiple phenotypes of DS, including lethal immune hypersensitivity, congenital heart defects (CHDs), cognitive impairments, and craniofacial anomalies.
source: In a mouse model of DS, normalization of IFNR gene copy number rescues multiple phenotypes of DS, including lethal immune hypersensitivity, congenital heart defects (CHDs), cognitive impairments, and craniofacial anomalies (Waugh et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: JAK inhibition rescues lethal immune hypersensitivity in mouse models of DS.
source: JAK inhibition rescues lethal immune hypersensitivity in these mouse models (Tuttle et al., 2020) and attenuates the global dysregulation of gene expression caused by the trisomy across multiple murine tissues (Galbraith et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Prenatal JAK inhibition in pregnant mice prevents the appearance of CHDs.
source: Furthermore, prenatal JAK inhibition in pregnant mice prevents the appearance of CHDs (Chi et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: T21 elicits an interferonopathy in DS.
source: Altogether, these results support the notion that T21 elicits an interferonopathy in DS, and that pharmacological inhibition of IFN signaling could have multiple therapeutic benefits in this population.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a conclusion based on cited evidence.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of IFN signaling could have multiple therapeutic benefits in DS.
source: Altogether, these results support the notion that T21 elicits an interferonopathy in DS, and that pharmacological inhibition of IFN signaling could have multiple therapeutic benefits in this population.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a conclusion based on cited evidence.

claim: The most common autoimmune condition in the HTP cohort is AITD, affecting 53.1% of the total cohort.
source: In this analysis, the most common autoimmune condition is AITD, affecting 53.1% of the total cohort (Figure 1a, Figure 1—figure supplement 1a, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the HTP cohort analysis, supported by data in Figure 1a.

claim: Autoimmune and inflammatory skin conditions represent the second most common category in the HTP cohort, affecting 43% of the cohort.
source: Grouped together, autoimmune and inflammatory skin conditions represent the second most common category, affecting 43% of the cohort, including: atopic dermatitis / eczema (27.9%), hidradenitis suppurativa / folliculitis / boils (20.6%), alopecia areata (7.7%), psoriasis (6.1%), and vitiligo (1.9%; Figure 1a, Figure 1—figure supplement 1b, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the HTP cohort analysis, supported by data in Figure 1a.

claim: The rate of celiac disease in the HTP cohort is 9.6%, which is highly elevated over that of the general population.
source: The rate of celiac disease (9.6%) is also highly elevated over that of the general population (Singh et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a finding from the HTP cohort analysis with a citation for comparison to the general population.

claim: 10 cases (2.2%) of juvenile Type I diabetes were observed in the HTP cohort.
source: We observed 10 cases (2.2%) of juvenile Type I diabetes, which has been reported to be more common in DS (Aitken et al., 2013; Johnson et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a finding from the HTP cohort analysis with supporting citations.

claim: Analysis of age trajectories of immune-related conditions in DS revealed early onset, with >80% of AITD, autoimmune/inflammatory skin conditions, and celiac disease being diagnosed in the first two decades of life.
source: Within the HTP cohort, analysis of age trajectories of immune-related conditions in DS revealed early onset, with >80% of AITD, autoimmune/inflammatory skin conditions, and celiac disease being diagnosed in the first two decades of life (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c–e).
evidence: This is a finding from the HTP cohort analysis, supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1c–e.

claim: The cumulative burden of autoimmunity and autoinflammation is similar in males versus females with DS, albeit with slightly increased rates of AITD and hidradenitis suppurativa in females.
source: The cumulative burden of autoimmunity and autoinflammation is similar in males versus females with DS, albeit with slightly increased rates of AITD and hidradenitis suppurativa in females (Figure 1—figure supplement 1f, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the HTP cohort analysis, supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1f.

claim: 75% of adult participants with DS had a history of at least one autoimmune/inflammatory condition (AITD, autoimmune/inflammatory skin conditions, or celiac disease).
source: In terms of co-occurrence, when evaluating the adult population (18+years old) for AITD, autoimmune/inflammatory skin conditions and celiac disease, we found that 75% of participants had a history of at least one condition, 38.4% had at least two, and 13.6% had three or more conditions (Figure 1b, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the HTP cohort analysis, supported by data in Figure 1b.

claim: 82.4% of adults with DS show positivity for anti-TPO or ANA, with 41.2% being positive for both.
source: Remarkably, 82.4% of adults with DS show positivity for at least one of these autoantibodies, with 41.2% being positive for both (Figure 1c, Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: This is a finding from autoantibody measurements in the HTP cohort, supported by data in Figure 1c.

claim: 62% of individuals with history of hypothyroidism were TPO+.
source: Indeed, 62% of individuals with history of hypothyroidism were TPO+, whereby anti-TPO is just one of the possible autoantibodies associated with AITD.
evidence: This is a finding from autoantibody measurements in the HTP cohort.

claim: 25 autoantibodies are significantly over-represented in people with DS relative to age- and sex-matched controls.
source: These efforts identified 25 autoantibodies significantly over-represented in people with DS relative to age- and sex-matched controls (Figure 1d), with 98.3% of individuals with DS being positive for at least one of these autoantibodies, and 63.3% being positive for six or more (Figure 1d–e).
evidence: This is a finding from autoantibody profiling using protein array technology, supported by data in Figure 1d.

claim: 98.3% of individuals with DS are positive for at least one of the 25 autoantibodies over-represented in DS.
source: These efforts identified 25 autoantibodies significantly over-represented in people with DS relative to age- and sex-matched controls (Figure 1d), with 98.3% of individuals with DS being positive for at least one of these autoantibodies, and 63.3% being positive for six or more (Figure 1d–e).
evidence: This is a finding from autoantibody profiling, supported by data in Figure 1d-e.

claim: Individuals with hypothyroidism are more likely to be positive for anti-TPO antibodies.
source: Expectedly, individuals with hypothyroidism are more likely to be positive for anti-TPO antibodies (Figure 1g–h).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of autoantibody positivity relative to co-occurring conditions, supported by data in Figure 1g-h.

claim: TPO+ status associates with higher rates of use of pressure equalizing (PE) tubes employed to alleviate the symptoms of recurrent ear infections and otitis media with effusion (OME).
source: However, unexpectedly, TPO+ status also associates with higher rates of use of pressure equalizing (PE) tubes employed to alleviate the symptoms of recurrent ear infections and otitis media with effusion (OME), which is common in DS (Elling et al., 2023, Figure 1g–h).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of autoantibody positivity relative to co-occurring conditions, supported by data in Figure 1g-h.

claim: Positivity for additional autoantibodies was more common in those with other co-occurring neurological conditions.
source: Positivity for additional autoantibodies was more common in those with other co-occurring neurological conditions, a broad classification encompassing various seizure disorders, movement disorders, and structural brain abnormalities (Figure 1g–h, Figure 1—figure supplement 1g).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of autoantibody positivity relative to co-occurring conditions, supported by data in Figure 1g-h.

claim: Individuals with history of tricuspid valve regurgitation display higher rates of four different autoantibodies, most prominently against WARS1 and SRP68.
source: Individuals with history of tricuspid valve regurgitation display higher rates of four different autoantibodies, most prominently against WARS1, a tryptophan tRNA synthetase mutated in various neurodevelopmental disorders (Lin et al., 2022), and SRP68, a protein commonly targeted by autoantibodies in necrotizing myopathies (Allenbach et al., 2020, Figure 1—figure supplement 1g).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of autoantibody positivity relative to co-occurring conditions, supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1g.

claim: Individuals with a history of frequent pneumonia present a higher frequency of autoantibodies against DSG3 (desmoglein 3).
source: Individuals with a history of frequent pneumonia present a higher frequency of autoantibodies against DSG3 (desmoglein 3), a cell adhesion molecule targeted by autoantibodies in paraneoplastic pemphigus (PNP), an autoimmune disease of the skin and mucous membranes that can involve fatal lung complications (Amagai et al., 1998, Figure 1g–h).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of autoantibody positivity relative to co-occurring conditions, supported by data in Figure 1g-h.

claim: Massive immune remodeling occurs in all major myeloid and lymphoid subsets in DS, including increases in basophils, along with depletion of eosinophils and total B cells.
source: In agreement with previous analyses (Waugh et al., 2019; Araya et al., 2019; Lambert et al., 2022; Galbraith et al., 2023; Malle et al., 2023), we observed massive immune remodeling in all major myeloid and lymphoid subsets, including increases in basophils, along with depletion of eosinophils and total B cells (Figure 2a-c, Figure 2—figure supplement 1a-c).
evidence: This is a finding from mass cytometry analysis, supported by data in Figure 2a-c and previous citations.

claim: Global immune changes in DS are largely independent of the presence of clinical diagnoses or autoantibody positivity.
source: When comparing various subgroups within the DS cohort based on autoimmunity status, we observed that these global immune changes are largely independent of the presence of clinical diagnoses or autoantibody positivity, with very few additional changes significantly associated with these measures of autoimmunity (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This is a finding from mass cytometry analysis comparing subgroups, supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d.

claim: The significant depletion of B cells and enrichment of basophils in DS is not significantly different among various autoimmunity subgroups.
source: For example, the significant depletion of B cells and enrichment of basophils in DS is not significantly different among the various subgroups (Figure 2c, Figure 2—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is a finding from mass cytometry analysis comparing subgroups, supported by data in Figure 2c.

claim: Non-classical monocytes are further elevated in the ANA+ group.
source: Among CD45+ CD66lo non-granulocytes, most changes are conserved among subgroups, with the sole of exception of non-classical monocytes, which are further elevated in the ANA+ group (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d–e).
evidence: This is a finding from mass cytometry analysis comparing subgroups, supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d-e.

claim: γδ T cells (both total and CD8+) are depleted in those with multiple autoimmune diagnoses.
source: Notably, we observed depletion of γδ T cells (both total and CD8+) in those with multiple autoimmune diagnoses (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d,f), a result that is in line with reports documenting depletion of these subsets from peripheral circulation toward sites of active autoimmunity (Amini et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a finding from mass cytometry analysis comparing subgroups, supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d,f and a citation.

claim: Age-associated B cells (ABCs) tend to be further elevated in the TPO+ group.
source: Among B cells, the overall shift toward more differentiated states such as plasmablasts, age-associated B cells (ABCs), and IgM+ memory cells is also conserved among subgroups, with the sole exception of ABCs, which tend to be further elevated in the TPO+ group (Figure 2g–i, Figure 2—figure supplement 1d,g).
evidence: This is a finding from mass cytometry analysis comparing subgroups, supported by data in Figure 2g-i.

claim: T21 causes global remodeling of the immune system toward an autoimmunity-prone and pro-inflammatory state, prior to clinically evident autoimmunity.
source: Altogether, these results indicate that T21 causes global remodeling of the immune system toward an autoimmunity-prone and pro-inflammatory state, prior to clinically evident autoimmunity, and dwarfing any additional effects associated with confirmed diagnoses of autoimmune/inflammatory conditions or common biomarkers of autoimmunity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mass cytometry analysis results.

claim: Individuals with DS display elevated levels of many inflammatory markers, including several interleukins, cytokines, and chemokines known to drive autoimmune conditions, such as IL-6 and TNF-α.
source: It is well established that individuals with DS display elevated levels of many inflammatory markers, including several interleukins, cytokines, and chemokines known to drive autoimmune conditions, such as IL-6 and TNF-α (Sullivan et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2017; Malle et al., 2023; Galbraith et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated as well-established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Profound hypercytokinemia occurs in DS, with significant elevation of multiple acute phase proteins, pro-inflammatory cytokines, and chemokines.
source: These efforts confirmed the notion of profound hypercytokinemia in DS (Sullivan et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2017; Malle et al., 2023; Galbraith et al., 2023), with significant elevation of multiple acute phase proteins (e.g. CRP, SAA, IL1RA), pro-inflammatory cytokines (TSLP, IL-17C, IL-22, IL-17D, IL-9, IL-6, TNF-α) and chemokines (IP-10, MIP-3a, MIP-1a, MCP-1, MCP-4, Eotaxin), as well as growth factors associated with inflammation and wound healing (FGF, PIGF, VEGF-A; Figure 3a).
evidence: This is a finding from plasma proteomics analysis, supported by data in Figure 3a and previous citations.

claim: No important differences in inflammatory markers were observed within the DS cohort based on various metrics of autoimmunity (number of autoimmune/inflammatory conditions, ANA or TPO positivity status, or number of other autoantibodies).
source: However, when evaluating for differences within the DS cohort based on various metrics of autoimmunity, we did not observe important differences based on number of autoimmune/inflammatory conditions, ANA or TPO positivity status, or number of other autoantibodies (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is a finding from plasma proteomics analysis comparing subgroups, supported by data in Figure 3a.

claim: CRP, IL-6, and TNF-α are equally elevated across all autoimmunity subgroups in DS.
source: For example, CRP, IL-6, and TNF-α are equally elevated across all these subgroups (Figure 3b–d, Figure 3—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is a finding from plasma proteomics analysis comparing subgroups, supported by data in Figure 3b-d.

claim: Many inflammatory factors elevated in DS across the lifespan do not display a significant increase with age, such as IL-9 and IL-17C.
source: We then compared the effects of age versus T21 status on cytokine levels in the DS cohort, which identified many inflammatory factors elevated in DS across the lifespan that do not display a significant increase with age, such as IL-9 and IL-17C, or that increase with age only in the DS cohort, such as IP-10 (Figure 3e–f, Figure 3—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of age effects on cytokine levels, supported by data in Figure 3e-f.

claim: T21 induces a constitutive hypercytokinemia from early childhood, with only a fraction of these inflammatory changes being exacerbated with age.
source: Altogether, these results indicate that T21 induces a constitutive hypercytokinemia from early childhood, with only a fraction of these inflammatory changes being exacerbated with age.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the plasma proteomics and age analysis results.

claim: IFN hyperactivity and downstream JAK/STAT signaling are key drivers of immune dysregulation in DS.
source: Several lines of evidence support the notion that IFN hyperactivity and downstream JAK/STAT signaling are key drivers of immune dysregulation in DS (Sullivan et al., 2016; Sullivan et al., 2017; Waugh et al., 2019; Araya et al., 2019; Powers et al., 2019; Tuttle et al., 2020; Chi et al., 2023; Galbraith et al., 2023; Waugh et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion supported by multiple citations.

claim: In mouse models of DS, both normalization of IFNR gene copy number and pharmacologic JAK1 inhibition rescue their lethal immune hypersensitivity phenotypes.
source: In mouse models of DS, both normalization of IFNR gene copy number and pharmacologic JAK1 inhibition rescue their lethal immune hypersensitivity phenotypes (Tuttle et al., 2020; Waugh et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: IFN transcriptional scores derived from peripheral immune cells correlate significantly with the degree of immune remodeling and hypercytokinemia in DS.
source: Furthermore, we recently demonstrated that IFN transcriptional scores derived from peripheral immune cells correlate significantly with the degree of immune remodeling and hypercytokinemia in DS (Galbraith et al., 2023), and we and others have reported the safe use of JAK inhibitors for treatment of diverse immune conditions in DS, including alopecia areata (Rachubinski et al., 2019), psoriatic arthritis (Pham et al., 2021) and hemophagocytic lymphohistocytosis (Guild et al., 2022) through small case series.
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: No adverse events were observed that required a change or cessation of tofacitinib dosing in the first 10 participants.
source: This analysis established that there were no AEs that required a change or cessation of tofacitinib dosing and that this medicine is well tolerated in individuals with DS.
evidence: This is a finding from the interim clinical trial analysis.

claim: Tofacitinib is well tolerated in individuals with DS.
source: This analysis established that there were no AEs that required a change or cessation of tofacitinib dosing and that this medicine is well tolerated in individuals with DS.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the interim clinical trial analysis.

claim: Seven of the ten participants had an improvement in the IGA score.
source: The interim analysis showed that seven of the ten participants had an improvement in the IGA score and eight of the ten reported some improvement on their life quality related to their skin condition as measured by the DLQI (Figure 5a-b, Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the interim clinical trial analysis, supported by data in Figure 5a-b.

claim: Eight of the ten participants reported some improvement on their life quality related to their skin condition as measured by the DLQI.
source: The interim analysis showed that seven of the ten participants had an improvement in the IGA score and eight of the ten reported some improvement on their life quality related to their skin condition as measured by the DLQI (Figure 5a-b, Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the interim clinical trial analysis, supported by data in Figure 5a-b.

claim: Five of six participants with alopecia areata showed scalp hair regrowth.
source: The most striking effects were observed for alopecia areata (Figure 5c-d, Figure 5—figure supplement 1a). Five of six participants with alopecia areata showed scalp hair regrowth, with the exception being a male participant (AA1) with history of alopecia totalis for 20+years who only showed facial hair and eyelash re-growth.
evidence: This is a finding from the interim clinical trial analysis, supported by data in Figure 5c-d.

claim: One participant with psoriasis due to psoriatic arthritis experienced an almost complete remission of psoriatic arthritis symptoms.
source: One participant presented with psoriasis due to psoriatic arthritis and experienced an almost complete remission of psoriatic arthritis symptoms (Ps1, Figure 5—figure supplement 1b–c).
evidence: This is a finding from the interim clinical trial analysis, supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1b-c.

claim: For the two participants that presented with atopic dermatitis, the clinical manifestations were markedly reduced during tofacitinib treatment.
source: For the two participants that presented with atopic dermatitis, the clinical manifestations were markedly reduced during tofacitinib treatment (Figure 5e–f).
evidence: This is a finding from the interim clinical trial analysis, supported by data in Figure 5e-f.

claim: At baseline, clinical trial participants show IFN scores within the typical range for DS, but values are decreased at 2, 8, and 16 weeks of tofacitinib treatment.
source: At baseline, clinical trial participants show IFN scores within the typical range for DS, but values are decreased at 2, 8, and 16 weeks of tofacitinib treatment (Figure 6a, Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the interim clinical trial analysis, supported by data in Figure 6a.

claim: Most participants show a decrease in IFN scores as soon as two weeks of treatment which is sustained over time.
source: Time course analysis revealed that most participants show a decrease in IFN scores as soon as two weeks of treatment which is sustained over time, with two clear exceptions (Figure 6—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is a finding from the interim clinical trial analysis, supported by data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1a.

claim: ISGs as a group are significantly downregulated upon tofacitinib treatment, but the effect is not uniform across all ISGs.
source: Collectively, ISGs as a group are significantly downregulated upon tofacitinib treatment, but the effect is not uniform across all ISGs (Figure 6c), indicating that JAK1/3 inhibition does not reduce all IFN signaling elevated in DS, which could be explained by the fact that the IFN pathways also employ JAK2 for signal transduction (Schwartz et al., 2016; Schwartz et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a finding from the interim clinical trial analysis, supported by data in Figure 6c and citations.

claim: Tofacitinib treatment reverses the dysregulation of many gene signatures observed in DS, effectively attenuating many pro-inflammatory signatures beyond IFN gamma and alpha responses.
source: Global analysis of transcriptome changes revealed that tofacitinib treatment reverses the dysregulation of many gene signatures observed in DS, effectively attenuating many pro-inflammatory signatures beyond IFN gamma and alpha responses, such as Inflammatory Response, TNF-α signaling via NFkB, IL-2 STAT5 signaling, and IL-6 JAK STAT3 signaling (Figure 6—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is a finding from the interim clinical trial analysis, supported by data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1c.

claim: At baseline, clinical trial participants show cytokine scores within the range observed for DS, but these values decrease at 2, 8 and 16 weeks relative to baseline.
source: At baseline, clinical trial participants show cytokine scores within the range observed for DS, but these values decrease at 2, 8 and 16 weeks relative to baseline (Figure 6d–e, Figure 6—figure supplement 1e, Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the interim clinical trial analysis, supported by data in Figure 6d-e.

claim: The decreases in TNF-α and IL-6 observed upon tofacitinib treatment indicate that elevation of these potent inflammatory cytokines requires sustained JAK/STAT signaling in DS.
source: The decreases in TNF-α and IL-6 observed upon tofacitinib treatment indicate that elevation of these potent inflammatory cytokines requires sustained JAK/STAT signaling in DS (Figure 6e).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the clinical trial results, supported by data in Figure 6e.

claim: Seven of the 10 participants presented at baseline with anti-TPO levels above the upper limit of normal (ULN, 60 U/mL), and all seven experienced a decrease in these auto-antibodies at 8 weeks and 16 weeks relative to baseline.
source: Seven of the 10 participants presented at baseline with anti-TPO levels above the upper limit of normal (ULN, 60 U/mL), and all seven experienced a decrease in these auto-antibodies at 8 weeks and 16 weeks relative to baseline (Figure 6f, Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the interim clinical trial analysis, supported by data in Figure 6f.

claim: For one participant (HS1) anti-TPO levels decreased below the ULN while on the trial.
source: In fact, for one participant (HS1) the levels decreased below the ULN while on the trial.
evidence: This is a finding from the interim clinical trial analysis.

claim: Three participants had anti-TG levels above the ULN (4 IU/mL) and all three showed a decrease from baseline levels while on tofacitinib at both 8 and 16 weeks.
source: Additionally, three of these seven participants also had anti-TG levels above the ULN (4 IU/mL) and all three showed a decrease from baseline levels while on tofacitinib at both 8 and 16 weeks, with one participant (AA6) falling below the ULN upon treatment (Figure 6f).
evidence: This is a finding from the interim clinical trial analysis, supported by data in Figure 6f.

claim: Tofacitinib treatment lowers IFN scores and cytokine levels to within the range observed in the general population, not below, indicating that this immunomodulatory strategy can provide therapeutic benefit in DS without overt immune suppression.
